subject: Northbridge discovery: budget constraints, token economics & batching options
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@northbridge.com>, Tom Whitaker <t.whitaker@northbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Northbridge discovery: budget constraints, token economics & batching options

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap while notes are fresh and to align on next steps: 

1) Key pain points you shared
- Latency-sensitive fraud-review and customer chat flows causing operational backlog at peak (3–5s target currently slipping)
- Token spend is the single largest month-to-month line item in model-enabled features; finance needs clarity on predictable TCO before committing to a pilot

2) Goals we discussed
- Run a 6-week pilot for the chat + fraud review use cases with a clear cost guardrail (monthly cap) and acceptance criteria: P95 latency <= 800ms and <10% increase in false positives
- Prove 3x gross token savings using batching/prefix caching + model family selection versus current baseline or demonstrate equivalent quality at lower per-token cost

3) Cost/TCO framing (back-of-envelope from call)
- Baseline: ~2.4B tokens/month across both flows (current vendor)
- Conservative Redwood baseline estimate: 0.85–1.1 USD per 1k effective tokens (depends on batching and KV cache hit rate)
- Savings levers we can apply in pilot: batching (continuous batching for short, bursty traffic), prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, and smaller mixed-precision model variants for batched echoable steps
- Early pilot estimate: a 35–55% reduction in per-token spend if batching + 40–60% cache hit is achievable; exact numbers depend on session lengths and prompt variability

4) Decisions / asks from you
- Confirm the monthly token budget cap you need us to design the pilot around (you mentioned $40k–$60k as a potential range — please confirm)
- Share the MA/procurement contact and any standard SLAs or security forms procurement needs (I saw procurement@northbridge.com on your org chart)
- Approve a short technical kickoff with Ben (30–45m) to capture traffic patterns for batching and cache heuristics

Attachments: I attached a one-page pilot worksheet and a short batching model sketch for transparency (see: northbridge_ma_reqs.xlsx, redwood_batching_model_v2.pdf).

Next steps (proposed)
- You confirm budget cap and procurement contact by Thu 29 Apr
- Ben to run a 30m traffic-pattern call the week of May 3rd
- Internal Redwood kickoff (we scope cost SLOs + rollout plan)

Appreciate the time — happy to jump on a quick call if anything here needs correction.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — this matches our notes well. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Budget cap: leadership comfortable starting a pilot with a $50k/month soft cap (we will reassess after month 1). That needs to include full inference run cost and any reserved capacity fees.
- Procurement: please route NDAs / MA to procurement@northbridge.com. They will need SOC2 + basic DPA language and a table of retention/window options (we are regulated, so data residency and retention windows are important).
- Acceptance criteria: in addition to the latency and FP targets, we will track cost per completed session for the chat flow specifically (baseline ~ $0.35/session).

Tom and I are available for the technical call — Thu 6 May or Mon 10 May afternoons ET. Please propose a slot.

Elena/Tom — quick technical notes ahead of the kickoff so we have alignment on what we'll measure and instrument: 

- Data we need (short): anonymized sample of 2–3 days of session-level traces (prompt lengths, avg tokens, user/session id hashed) + distribution of burst windows (per minute requests). That will let us simulate realistic batching and KV cache hit rates.
- Pilot configuration samples:
  * Option A (latency-first): small batching window (10–25ms), stronger KV caching on repeated prompts, mid-sized quantized model variant — target P95 <= 800ms
  * Option B (cost-first): larger batching window (50–150ms), more aggressive quantization + sharded KV cache, target 40–55% token cost reduction but expect some tail latency degradation
- Measurement plan: we will instrument request-level token billing, cache-hit ratio, effective tokens-per-session, and compute per-session cost (USD). I will provide a spreadsheet with simulation cells (attached).

Attachments: redwood_batching_model_v2.pdf (walkthrough) and a sample instrumentation CSV.

I can take the Thu 6 May 2:30–3:15pm ET slot if you confirm — otherwise Mon 10 May works as well.
